ai.description: *Cnemaspis beddomei* is a small gecko reaching 40 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a series of dark dorsal spots and a distinct yellow-tipped tail. Key features include keeled ventral scales and digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis beddomei* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, keeled mid-dorsal tubercles that extend from the nape to the tail base.
ai.habitat: Cnemaspis beddomei inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on rock surfaces and tree trunks at elevations of 600–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome’s Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: Cnemaspis beddomei is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cnemaspis beddomei is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
